hook.line: Cafés have debts, bosses have crises and essays have problems that need an answer. Spanish has a calm, slightly formal way to say you are dealing with them head on.
hook.es: La cooperativa tuvo que hacer frente a una deuda enorme.
hook.en: The cooperative had to face a huge debt.

examples.es: La cooperativa tuvo que hacer frente a una deuda enorme.
examples.en: The cooperative had to face a huge debt.

examples.es: No sé cómo vamos a afrontar estos gastos.
examples.en: I don't know how we're going to cope with these expenses.

examples.es: Tomás hizo frente a la crisis con calma.
¿Cómo hacen frente a los gastos del café?
examples.en: How do you all meet the café's expenses?

examples.es: El barrio debe afrontar un cambio enorme.
examples.en: The neighbourhood has to face an enormous change.

examples.es: Para hacer frente al problema, necesitamos más tiempo.
examples.en: To deal with the problem, we need more time.

rule:
*Hacer frente a* means to face a difficulty and deal with it: a debt, a crisis, expenses, a problem.

*Hacer* changes like any verb (*hizo frente*, *hace frente*, *hará frente*), but *frente a* stays put. Before *el* it becomes *al*: *hacer frente al problema*.

*Afrontar* means almost the same, but it takes no *a*: *afrontar los gastos*, *afrontar una crisis*.

With money, both mean "to cover" or "to meet" the costs. English "face" or "cope with" is the closest match. For a rival it means "stand up to": *hacer frente a Altamira*. For a building that faces the park, Spanish uses another verb: *da al parque*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *hacer frente a* a *locución verbal*: a verb phrase that works as one unit.

readAndPick.es: La cooperativa tuvo que hacer frente a una deuda enorme.
options: The cooperative had to face a huge debt.
The cooperative had a huge debt in front of it.
The cooperative made a huge debt.

readAndPick.es: No sé cómo vamos a afrontar estos gastos.
options: I don't know how we avoided these expenses.
I don't know how we're going to cope with these expenses.
I don't know who is paying these expenses.

readAndPick.es: Tomás hizo frente a la crisis con calma.
options: Tomás ran away from the crisis.
Tomás will face the crisis calmly.
Tomás faced the crisis calmly.

readAndPick.es: ¿Cómo hacen frente a los gastos del café?
options: How do you all meet the café's expenses?
How did you all avoid the café's expenses?
Why do you all have the café's expenses?

readAndPick.es: El barrio debe afrontar un cambio enorme.
options: The neighbourhood must avoid an enormous change.
The neighbourhood must face an enormous change.
The neighbourhood caused an enormous change.

readAndPick.es: Para hacer frente al problema, necesitamos más tiempo.
options: To deal with the problem, we need more time.
The problem needs more time to arrive.
We need more time to forget the problem.

readAndPick.es: Hernando no puede hacer frente a tantas deudas.
options: Hernando can't cope with so many debts.
Hernando doesn't owe anything.
Hernando can pay all his debts.

readAndPick.es: Vale afronta cada día con una sonrisa.
options: Vale avoids each day with a smile.
Vale faces each day with a smile.
Vale smiled at each day yesterday.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *hacer frente a* or *hacer frente* and type the whole sentence: *La cooperativa tuvo que ___ una deuda enorme.*
yourTurn.answer: La cooperativa tuvo que hacer frente a una deuda enorme.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I don't know how we're going to cope with these expenses.
yourTurn.answer: No sé cómo vamos a afrontar estos gastos.
accept: No sé cómo vamos a hacer frente a estos gastos.
yourTurn.why: *Afrontar* takes the expenses directly, with no *a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Tomás faced the crisis calmly.
yourTurn.answer: Tomás hizo frente a la crisis con calma.
accept: Tomás afrontó la crisis con calma.
yourTurn.why: *Hizo* is the past of *hacer*, and *frente a* stays as it is.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: To deal with the problem, we need more time.
yourTurn.answer: Para hacer frente al problema, necesitamos más tiempo.
accept: Necesitamos más tiempo para hacer frente al problema.

yourTurn.prompt: Say the same with *afrontar*: *Tomás hizo frente a la crisis.* Say: Tomás faced the crisis.
yourTurn.why: *Afrontar* carries the idea itself, so it needs no *frente* and no *a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The neighbourhood has to face an enormous change.
yourTurn.answer: El barrio debe afrontar un cambio enorme.
accept: El barrio tiene que afrontar un cambio enorme.
El barrio debe hacer frente a un cambio enorme.
El barrio tiene que hacer frente a un cambio enorme.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Hernando can't cope with so many debts.
yourTurn.answer: Hernando no puede hacer frente a tantas deudas.
accept: Hernando no puede afrontar tantas deudas.
yourTurn.why: *No puede* comes first, then the phrase as usual.

pitfalls.wrong: Hizo frente la crisis con calma.
pitfalls.right: Hizo frente a la crisis con calma.

pitfalls.wrong: No sé cómo vamos a afrontar a estos gastos.
pitfalls.right: No sé cómo vamos a afrontar estos gastos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Afrontar* takes its object directly, with no *a*.

pitfalls.wrong: Tuvo que hacer frente de una deuda.
pitfalls.right: Tuvo que hacer frente a una deuda.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The preposition is always *a*, never *de*.

personal: Say one difficulty you've had to face lately, using *hacer frente a* or *afrontar*.
